title: Philadelphia Fed November 2026 Nonmanufacturing Business Outlook Survey — 8:30 a.m. ET, the services half of the Q4 PIES input, published the calendar day before it
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events?release=manufacturing-business-outlook-survey, fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200, 130,695 bytes) — the Philadelphia Fed's own release calendar, whose embedded structured data carries the row verbatim as `{"title":"November Nonmanufacturing Business Outlook Survey","day":"24","displayMonth":"Nov","year":"2026","time":"8:30 a.m."}`. The same payload enumerates all twelve 2026 NBOS editions (Jan 20 · Feb 24 · Mar 24 · Apr 21 · May 26 · Jun 23 · Jul 21 · Aug 25 · Sep 22 · Oct 20 · Nov 24 · Dec 22), each exactly three business days after that month's MBOS, plus a `Historical Revisions: Nonmanufacturing Business Outlook Survey, Jan 13 2026` row. Identical surface at identical reliability to the three philly-fed-mfg entries this calendar already rests on. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only). Discovered 2026-09-10 in the never-assessed initial research of philly-fed-mfg-2026-11-19
notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the philly-fed-mfg-2026-11-19 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-10. IT DEPARTS FROM TWO SIBLING DECLINES AND THE REASON IS SPECIFIC, not a change of taste. philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15's ledger declined the NBOS as a second-order survey and philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17's ledger declined philly-fed-nbos-2026-12-22 'on the same second-order-survey grounds... kept consistent deliberately'. Neither decline covers this edition, because the 11-24 NBOS has an upstream role the December one does not: the Q4 2026 Price and Inflation Expectations Survey (philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25, tracked as a proposal) publishes the CALENDAR DAY AFTER it, and that construction rule is reproduced 4 for 4 from the single enumerated payload cited above — Feb 24 NBOS then Feb 25 PIES, May 26 then May 27, Aug 25 then Aug 26, Nov 24 then Nov 25, every PIES at 10:00 a.m. and every NBOS at 8:30 a.m. So the Q4 PIES's two dated inputs are the 11-19 MBOS (this proposer, the manufacturing half) and the 11-24 NBOS (the services half), and this calendar currently carries neither as the PIES ledger's upstream. The December NBOS has no such role: the Q4 PIES has already published by 12-22. WHOEVER WRITES THE CANONICAL FILE OWNS (a) deciding whether the PIES-upstream argument actually survives contact with the PIES ledger, which may well read its own inputs differently, and (b) re-verifying the date and time against an NBOS-specific surface rather than the shared calendar row — noting that this session could not do so for the MANUFACTURING survey either, because the MBOS landing page's Release Calendar panel publishes only the next release, and the same limitation is expected here. A DECLINE with reasoning recorded is an acceptable outcome and would simply restore the two siblings' consistency. Impact LOW and symbols [] provisionally, matched to the regional-survey class rather than re-litigated by a lane that does not own it. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE: it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the proposing ledger registers no forward test that depends on it.
